source.title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning

observations.text: WorldEvolver's Selective Foresight is an explicit post-prediction abstention gate: episodic memory is retrieved, the frozen world model predicts a next observation with confidence q_t, and the prediction is exposed to the frozen agent only when q_t >= tau; otherwise F_t is the empty signal. The agent and world-model parameters remain frozen.

The paper's oracle diagnostic establishes the risk of indiscriminate prediction exposure under a fixed Gemma-4-26B-A4B agent/backbone: on ScienceWorld action accuracy is 0.271 with no foresight, 0.251 with noisy foresight, and 0.281 with perfect foresight; on ALFWorld the corresponding values are 0.385, 0.344, and 0.493. Thus a prediction can be worse than abstaining when it is unreliable.

AgentBoard planning compares the same WorldEvolver memory framework with and without Selective Foresight while keeping the agent/backbone fixed. The paper reports Selective Foresight improves or ties the no-foresight variant in all eight agent/backbone/environment cells. On ScienceWorld the four w/o-F -> w/F pairs are 46.67->52.22, 62.22->63.33, 48.89->50.00, and 62.22->63.33.

This is stronger science-environment evidence for abstention-aware exposure than pure retrieval ablations because the gate acts after a prediction has already been produced from the memory-conditioned world model. However, w/o F_t is no foresight rather than an always-expose-unfiltered condition, and ScienceWorld is an interactive science benchmark rather than an autonomous research workflow.

protocol_inferences.name: POST_PREDICTION_SIGNAL_EXPOSURE_SHOULD_SUPPORT_EMPTY_OUTPUT
protocol_inferences.text: A generated/retrieved scientific-support signal should not acquire downstream influence merely because it exists. The exposure layer should be able to emit an empty signal when confidence/admissibility is insufficient.

protocol_inferences.name: GATE_EFFECT_EVALUATION_MUST_DISTINGUISH_NO_SIGNAL_FROM_ALWAYS_EXPOSE
protocol_inferences.text: A selective-gate versus no-signal comparison supports the usefulness of gated assistance but does not by itself measure the safety benefit over always exposing every candidate. Report these causal contrasts separately.

phase1_acceptance.reason: WorldEvolver is useful science-environment evidence for post-prediction selective exposure but requires model/environment execution and does not provide a zero-dependency scheduled-Chat completion route.

scope_notes: Do not call the ScienceWorld result an autonomous-scientist research result; it is agent planning in a science environment.
Do not claim Table 2 compares selective exposure against always-unfiltered exposure; it compares w/F_t against w/o F_t.
Use the oracle noisy-foresight diagnostic as risk evidence and the w/F_t comparison as gated-assistance evidence, not as one single matched always-expose ablation.
